nodes.summary: Cycle lemma (Dvoretzky–Motzkin 1947). If `x : Fin n → ℕ` satisfies `∑ x_i + k = n` with `1 ≤ k`, then exactly `k` of the `n` cyclic shifts of `x` (counted by shift `r < n`) are first-passage sequences.
nodes.title: Cycle lemma

nodes.summary: For Poisson(`r`) offspring and one ancestor, the total progeny satisfies `P(T = n) = e^{-rn} (rn)^{n-1} / n!` for `n ≥ 1` (Borel 1942).
nodes.title: Borel law

nodes.summary: The weight `H_p(k, n) = ∑ ∏_i p(x_i)` over the step sequences with `∑ x_i + k = n` along which the walk from `k` first hits `0` at time `n`. For `p(j) = P(ξ = j)` this is the probability `P(T = n)` that the total progeny of `k` ancestors is `n`.
nodes.title: Hitting weight of first-passage step sequences

nodes.summary: The exploration walk started at `k` with steps `x_i - 1` stays positive at every time `j < n`: `j < k + ∑_{i < j} x_i`. Together with `∑ x_i + k = n` this says that the walk first hits `0` at time `n`.
nodes.title: First passage of the exploration walk

nodes.summary: The mean total progeny is `(1 - m)⁻¹` in `[0, ∞]`: it is `1 / (1 - m)` for `m < 1` and `∞` for `m ≥ 1` (`m` the mean offspring number).
nodes.title: Mean total progeny equals $1/(1-m)$

nodes.summary: The mean total progeny `∑_n E Z_n` of the Galton–Watson process started from one individual. By Tonelli this is `E ∑_n Z_n` for any process with the generation laws `law ν n`.
nodes.title: Mean total progeny of a Galton–Watson process

nodes.summary: Under `ν^{⊗n}`, the event that the walk from `k` first hits `0` at time `n` has measure `H_p(k, n)` with `p(j) = ν{j}`. When `ν` is a probability measure this is the probability `P(T = n)`.
nodes.title: Probability of first passage at time n

nodes.summary: Under `ν^{⊗n}`, the event `ξ_1 + ⋯ + ξ_n + k = n` has measure `W_p(k, n)` with `p(j) = ν{j}`. When `ν` is a probability measure this is the probability `P(ξ_1 + ⋯ + ξ_n = n - k)`.
nodes.title: Probability of the offspring walk event as a walk weight

nodes.summary: For Poisson(`r`) offspring and `k ≤ n` ancestors, `n · P(T = n) = k e^{-rn} (rn)^{n-k} / (n-k)!` (Tanner 1961; Haight–Breuer 1960).
nodes.title: Borel–Tanner law

nodes.summary: Hitting-time theorem, weighted form: `n · H_p(k, n) = k · W_p(k, n)` for every weight `p` with values in a commutative semiring and all `k, n`. For probability weights this is the hitting-time theorem of van der Hofstad–Keane (2008); the proof double counts cyclic shifts with the cycle lemma.
nodes.title: Hitting-time theorem

nodes.summary: For i.i.d. offspring numbers with law `ν` and `k` ancestors, the finite-measure identity `n · P(T = n) = k · P(ξ_1 + ⋯ + ξ_n = n - k)` holds as an identity of event masses (Otter 1949; Dwass 1969); the two sides are probabilities when `ν` is a probability measure.
nodes.title: Otter–Dwass formula

nodes.summary: The cyclic shift `i ↦ x_{(i + r) mod n}` of a tuple.
nodes.title: Cyclic shift of a tuple

nodes.summary: For Poisson(`r`) step weights, `W_p(k, n) = e^{-rn} (rn)^{n-k} / (n-k)!` when `k ≤ n`: the sum of `n` independent Poisson(`r`) variables is Poisson(`rn`).
nodes.title: Walk weights for Poisson offspring

nodes.summary: The weight `W_p(k, n) = ∑ ∏_i p(x_i)` over the step sequences `x : Fin n → ℕ` with `∑ x_i + k = n` (the walk from `k` is at `0` at time `n`). For `p(j) = P(ξ = j)` this is `P(ξ_1 + ⋯ + ξ_n = n - k)` when `k ≤ n`, and `0` when `k > n`.
nodes.title: Walk weight of step sequences ending at zero
